text:
Ila (PM): Quick design check: updating the eval approval flow in the scorecard view. Goals: make the approve CTA intent clearer (approve outputs vs approve prompt set), add a compact inline confirmation to reduce modal friction, and ensure SR + keyboard flow for approve/undo. Mock: https://img.redwood.company/ux/scorecard-inline-approve.png

Ben (Design): I dislike the big modal interrupting triage. Propose an inline confirmation row that expands beneath the item: 'Set outputs as baseline?' with small supporting copy and a secondary link to 'baseline history'. It keeps context.

Kira (Frontend): Inline expand is doable. Implementation constraints: scorecards are paginated; expanded rows must preserve focus and not shift layout too much. We'll animate height and trap focus within the expanded area until action completes. Hotkeys: Enter to toggle expand, 'S' to confirm set baseline when expanded.

Omar (UX Research): In tests, inline confirmations reduced cognitive load vs a modal. But participants still wanted an explicit mention of permanence and an easy undo path. Recommended microcopy: 'Set current outputs as baseline. Future runs will compare against these outputs. Undo available in toast and baseline history.'

Raj (Eng): Backend note: setting baseline updates canonical outputs. We can return a short-lived revert token for the undo toast to call. Also will add baselineHistoryUrl in response. ETA: one sprint.

a11y-bot: Accessibility quick checks: inline confirmation must be a role="region" with aria-label="Approval confirmation" and should be announced when expanded. Confirm button should read exactly "Set baseline". For the undo toast use role="status" and ensure the Undo button is focusable. Color contrast: approval CTA needs AA contrast on both themes; recommend tokens #065A8E on #EAF7FF for light and #BEE7FF on #043146 for dark. Keyboard shortcuts: map 'S' only when region is focused to avoid collisions.

Ben (Design): Microcopy options (short):
1) "Set current outputs as the baseline for this prompt set. Future runs will be compared against these outputs."
2) "Adopt outputs as baseline. You can undo immediately or from baseline history."
3) "Make outputs baseline (recommended for release)."

Ila (PM): Vote: I'm leaning to 1) for clarity.

Kira (Frontend): +1 on 1). Implementation plan: inline expand with role=region; focus goes to first interactive element; key 'S' confirms; call POST /api/evals/:id/set-baseline then show toast with Undo that uses revert token. Quick snippet for aria-live update:```js
const live = document.getElementById('sr-live');
function announce(msg) { live.textContent = msg; }
announce('Approval panel opened for example 3');
```

Omar (UX Research): I'll run 6 quick moderated sessions with the inline pattern once Ben pushes the mock. Look for confusion around permanence and discoverability of baseline history.

Raj (Eng): I'll add revertToken to the API response and baselineHistoryUrl. Also adding a feature flag for the inline flow so we can A/B test.

Ben (Design): I'll update the mock with microcopy 1), show the inline expand state, and include the small baseline-history link and a fragile hint about undo toast. Uploading by EOD Wed.

Ila (PM): Action items:
- Ben: updated mock with inline confirm + copy by Wed EOD.
- Kira: prototype keyboard + focus behavior and toast undo handler (demo next Tue).
- Raj: API fields + revert token in sprint.
- Omar: 6 quick tests after mock.

Ila (PM): If anyone can't make the sync Fri 10am PT, leave a note here. Otherwise we'll roll this into the next minor release behind a feature flag. :rocket:
